version.changelog: Remove all sensitive field names from scripts and references to pass security scan

vt.analysis:
Type: OpenClaw Skill
Name: new-agent
Version: 1.5.0

The skill provides a legitimate interactive workflow for creating and configuring new OpenClaw agents across various messaging platforms (Telegram, Discord, etc.). It uses a helper script (scripts/setup-agent.sh) to scaffold local workspaces and standard openclaw CLI commands for registration, with no evidence of malicious intent, data exfiltration, or unauthorized execution.

llm.summary: The skill's files and script largely match the described purpose (creating agents and scaffolding workspaces), but the runtime instructions encourage pasting channel credentials into the conversation and the helper script copies the user's gateway config (which may contain secrets) — these behaviors increase risk and deserve caution.

dimensions.detail: Name, description, SKILL.md, README, channel guide, and the setup script all align: they create a workspace, register an agent, and describe how to bind channel credentials. No unrelated env vars or binaries are requested.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: references/channel-setup.md and SKILL.md explicitly tell the user to 'Paste it here' (i.e., paste platform bot tokens/credentials into the chat). Asking users to paste secrets into an agent conversation is unnecessary for setup and risks credential exposure or retention by the agent. The SKILL.md also tells the agent/user to add entries to openclaw.json but does not constrain how the agent should handle credentials, leaving room for accidental exfiltration.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: No install spec (instruction-only) and no remote downloads — minimal install risk. The included script is small and local; nothing is fetched from external URLs.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill declares no required env vars or credentials. The script uses OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR optionally (reasonable). However the script copies the gateway config file (openclaw.json) to a timestamped backup in the same directory, which may contain model tokens or channel credentials; creating backups without explicit guidance about handling sensitive fields is notable.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: always is false and the skill is user-invocable only. The script creates files under ~/.openclaw and registers the agent via openclaw CLI — these are expected for the purpose. Still, the script's backup of openclaw.json increases the on-disk footprint of potentially sensitive configuration.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: This skill appears to do what it claims (scaffold agent workspaces and walk you through channel binding), but exercise caution before providing any secrets in chat. Do not paste bot tokens, OAuth secrets, or service-account JSON directly into a conversation unless you understand how the agent will store and use them. Instead: (1) run the included setup script locally after inspecting it; it only creates workspace files and makes a backup of openclaw.json — verify the backup does not leak secrets to other users or locations; (2) prefer adding channel credentials directly to your local openclaw.json or use the OpenClaw CLI commands (openclaw channels login) rather than sending tokens to the agent; (3) if you must provide credentials to an agent, create scoped/limited tokens or ephemeral credentials, and rotate them afterwards; (4) review ~/.openclaw/openclaw.json for sensitive fields after running the script and securely delete any backups you don't want retained. If the skill's author can explain why credentials must be pasted into the chat (and show where/how they are stored and protected), that would reduce the risk and could change this assessment.
